_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md. Regen steps: re-apply ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/bitdefender/handfix/ (patch_*.py + internal/cli files) after any regen.

handfixes.summary: a client hook turns each /v1.x/jsonrpc/<area>#<method> call into a JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and unwraps result/error
handfixes.why: GravityZone's Public API is JSON-RPC 2.0 with no OpenAPI. The authored spec writes one POST path per method with the method name in the URL fragment, which net/http never sends. jsonrpc_transport.go (registered through registerClientHook, so it wraps every CLI and MCP client) builds the envelope from the fragment plus the generated command's body and returns the result member, or the error member as an HTTP error status. Without it every call posts bare params to the area URL and Control Center rejects it. Handwritten file from the factory's handfix/internal/cli; re-apply ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/bitdefender/handfix/ after any regen. The transport also refuses plain http:// to any non-loopback host before sending, since every request carries the API key as HTTP Basic (Codex review 2026-10-19, P1). The client hook also rejects a plain-HTTP base URL as a config error (exit 10) so no command retries it as a network failure.

handfixes.summary: the generated tail command is removed
handfixes.why: tail polls GET list endpoints. Every GravityZone method is a JSON-RPC POST, so the generator emits tail with an empty resource map that can only ever answer that there are no tail resources, and verify fails its resource-path check. handfix/patch_remove_tail.py deletes internal/cli/tail.go and its root.go registration; re-apply ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/bitdefender/handfix/ after any regen.

handfixes.summary: credential-precedence tests decode the HTTP Basic payload before asserting which key won
handfixes.why: The generated credentials_test.go asserts the raw secret appears in AuthHeader(), but GravityZone uses HTTP Basic with the API key as the username and an empty password, so the header is "Basic " + base64("<key>:") and the substring check fails. handfix/patch_credentials_test.py decodes the payload first (same fix datto-bcdr and wordpress carry); re-apply ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/bitdefender/handfix/ after any regen.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and guide.md say writes run immediately (no prompt), the local store holds fleet snapshots (no sync/search), and fleet health --fail-on exits 1; --dry-run is described as printing the JSON-RPC method and params (not the wire request); the MCP surface and read-only switch are described as they behave
handfixes.why: The generator's boilerplate promised sync/search commands that do not exist and an explicit --yes confirmation that generated write commands never ask for. handfix/patch_docs.py corrects the press README (vendored here as guide.md), SKILL.md and AGENTS.md; onboard re-vendors all three, so re-apply ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/bitdefender/handfix/ after any regen and re-run onboard. The msp-skills onboard also corrected, in the re-vendored SKILL.md and guide.md: --dry-run prints the method in the URL fragment plus bare params, not the JSON-RPC body sent on the wire; the API methods are reached over MCP through bitdefender_search/bitdefender_execute, not one MCP tool each; meta.source now tracks the real source for fleet locate and fleet rmm-gap; and guide.md documents BITDEFENDER_MCP_READ_ONLY. Re-apply these after any re-vendor.

handfixes.summary: the MCP bundle manifest declares BITDEFENDER_BASE_URL as an optional, non-secret field with the cloud default; server.json declares it optional and non-secret
handfixes.why: The generator ships only the API key in the .mcpb manifest, so Claude Desktop users on another region or an on-premises Control Center had no way to point the server at their Access URL. handfix/patch_manifest_base_url.py adds bitdefender_base_url (required false, default https://cloud.gravityzone.bitdefender.com/api) and maps it to BITDEFENDER_BASE_URL; re-apply ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/bitdefender/handfix/ after any regen.

handfixes.summary: Under BITDEFENDER_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 bitdefender_read runs only an explicit list of GravityZone read methods; reads that return or take a credential and every bitdefender_execute call stay refused (press 4.35.1 splits reads from writes and let its read tool run every read under the switch)
handfixes.why: The generated read-only switch refuses every non-GET execute call. Every GravityZone method is a JSON-RPC POST, so read-only mode refused reads too and an agent that should only read could not list a single endpoint. gz_readonly.go lists the get/find methods that only read (fail-closed: a method added by a later regeneration stays refused until listed) and leaves out the reads that return or take a credential: getPushEventSettings, getLicenseInfo, getCompanyDetailsByUser, getPackageDetails, getInstallationLinks, getIntegrationDetails, getPolicyDetails (password-protection and power-user password fields, per the vendor method page) and getNetworkInventoryItems (company items can carry license keys). The check reads the endpoint's registered path template, never the resolved path. A reprint restores the method-only check and silently re-breaks reads. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): reads now go through bitdefender_read and writes through bitdefender_execute; the generated switch refused every execute call but let bitdefender_read run push.get, license.get, policies.get and the other excluded reads. gravityZoneReadOnlyRefusesRead closes that (Codex r1 P2 'allowed MCP reads rejected' found the shape change); TestReadOnlySwitchRunsListedReadsAndRefusesCredentialReads failed on the pre-fix tree (push.get ran).

handfixes.summary: fleet locate and fleet rmm-gap set the agent envelope's meta.source to local when a saved snapshot answered
handfixes.why: Both commands carry pp:data-source auto, which the generated envelope reports as live, so a snapshot answer was labelled live in meta.source while results.source said snapshot. inventoryAgentSource maps the inventory's real source onto flags.agentSource before printing.

handfixes.summary: an env-sourced BITDEFENDER_BASE_URL is marked as an env override in config.Load and configForSave writes the file's own value back, so config.toml never captures the override
handfixes.why: The generated configForSave restored only the env-sourced API key, so `auth set-token` run with BITDEFENDER_BASE_URL set wrote that one-run URL into config.toml. After that, unsetting the variable had no effect and every later call sent the saved API key to the old host. Reproduced 2026-10-16 (config.toml carried base_url = the env value after set-token). internal/config/env_base_url_test.go fails with the restore lines removed. Same generator defect threatdown carries as env-urls-never-persisted.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: configForSave should restore every env-overridden field, not only credentials.

handfixes.summary: each fleet health company row carries status ok or fetch_failed, a field --compact (--agent) keeps
handfixes.why: A company whose getEndpointsList failed was still a ranked row with zero counts, and --agent (--compact) strips the row's error field, so an agent read it as a clean customer. Found by the 2026-10-16 adversarial review (round 1, P1). status survives compaction; gz_fleet_test.go TestFleetHealthFailedRowStatus fails if the failed row is marked ok.

handfixes.summary: bitdefender_execute substitutes the {service} path parameter for quarantine.list, quarantine.remove and quarantine.empty
handfixes.why: The generated code-orchestration registry gave the three quarantine/{service} methods an empty Positional list, so bitdefender_execute never substituted {service} and every call failed with 'unresolved path parameter {service}' (quarantine list could not run over MCP at all). The value is path-escaped, so a '#' cannot change the JSON-RPC method (verified: service='computers#createEmptyQuarantineTask' reached the server as quarantine/computers%23createEmptyQuarantineTask with method getQuarantineItemsList).

handfixes.why: Generated text sent agents to an always-empty resources table (there is no sync command), claimed a policies create command that does not exist while hiding the set-modules write. Found by the 2026-10-16 adversarial review (round 1, P2).

handfixes.summary: doctor probes general#getApiKeyDetails with the configured key and classifies the answer, instead of calling any response to GET / reachable and printing 'present, not verified'
handfixes.why: check_doctor_truth (issue #282) failed: the generated doctor printed the same verdict for a working key, a rejected key and a base_url aimed at the console's web UI. GravityZone has no GET endpoints, so doctor_verdict.go posts one JSON-RPC getApiKeyDetails call (no parameters, answered for any valid key) without a #method fragment, so the strict JSON-RPC transport passes it through and the raw status and envelope can be classified: a result is valid; a JSON-RPC error, 401, 404, 5xx or a non-envelope body is negative, and a 404 also marks the api row as not the Control Center API root. Only a JSON-RPC result counts: a 2xx list envelope is NOT accepted (Codex review 2026-10-16, P1: a wrong base answering {"items":[]} would read as valid); because GravityZone has no argument-free GET endpoint, that verdict says so, which is the honest negative check_doctor_truth allows for the healthy stub. doctor_verdict_test.go covers each case; check_doctor_truth --slug bitdefender fails without the wiring.

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http bearer token is read through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved ${user_config.bitdefender_mcp_http_token} placeholder refuses to start instead of becoming the secret
handfixes.why: The generated requireHTTPCallerToken read BITDEFENDER_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN with os.Getenv. The variable is declared as an optional MCPB user_config value, and a host that skips an optional prompt leaves the literal placeholder text in the environment; that text is public (it is in manifest.json), so anyone could authenticate to an HTTP-mode server started that way. Same fix as sophos-central. TestHTTPTokenPlaceholderRefused fails when the read goes back to os.Getenv.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: the press main_mcp.go.tmpl should read the HTTP token through cliutil.EnvOverride for every connector.

handfixes.summary: --client-profile is documented as inert on this connector and kept out of MCP tool schemas
handfixes.why: No tenant-gated client profile source is registered for GravityZone, so the flag changes nothing; the generated help promised tenant gating it does not provide, and an agent could believe it had scoped itself. The help now says so and the MCP schema no longer offers it. manifest.json and server.json describe PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE the same way.

handfixes.summary: every variable the binaries read (API key, base URL, user agent, MCP read-only switch, MCP HTTP token, client profile) is declared identically in manifest.json, server.json and every mcp-install.md env block
handfixes.why: check_env_schema failed: the generated manifest declared only the API key and base URL, so the .mcpb install could not turn on BITDEFENDER_MCP_READ_ONLY (the adversarial review's P2) and server.json marked the optional base URL as a required secret with no default. A regenerated manifest drops the extra user_config prompts. 2026-10-22: the read-only switch is preset to "1" in every mcp-install.md config block by the interim security note.

handfixes.summary: fleet rmm-gap's human output says INCOMPLETE instead of 'No gaps' when any GravityZone fetch failed
handfixes.why: With a company fetch failed and the supplied devices matching the companies that were read, the human output printed 'No gaps: N devices and M endpoints line up.' - a clean verdict over an incomplete comparison (Codex review 2026-10-16, P1). The JSON output already carried inventory_complete:false and fetch_failures.

handfixes.summary: the generator's hidden 'create' alias is removed from the 17 non-create commands that carried it
handfixes.why: Every GravityZone method is a JSON-RPC POST, so the press gave each POST command it could not name a create alias. The aliases were hidden from agent-context, SKILL.md and the governance tier table, yet 'tasks create' ran network#deleteTask, 'isolation create' isolated machines and 'policies create' / 'push create' / 'inventory create' ran Credential-tier reads, so a human approving a 'create' could be approving a delete and a name-keyed agent deny rule was bypassable. Found by the 2026-10-19 adversarial review (round 4, P2). Same class td-synnex removed. Press 4.35.1 gives the alias to four other non-create commands (inventory roots, policies set-modules, push reset-stats, tasks gather-logs); bin/reapply.py removes it from every non-create command.

handfixes.summary: the MCP context tool describes the real surface (JSON-RPC POST via bitdefender_search/bitdefender_execute, page/perPage paging, no sync or search tool, no CRM playbook) and the sql tool reports the latest fleet snapshot as ready or partial
handfixes.why: The generated context tool, which tells agents to call it first, claimed cursor paging with after/limit (default 100), a sync command and a full-text search tool, and typed endpoint tools. None exist here: GravityZone pages with page/perPage (default 30) and the only API tool is the untyped bitdefender_execute, so an agent following the tips sent invalid params or trusted a 30-row first page as complete. The sql tool also returned store_status empty while gz_fleet_runs held snapshots. Found by the 2026-10-19 adversarial review (round 4, P1 + P2). Round 5 (2026-10-19) found two CRM playbook entries ('sync first', 'search for contacts') and archetype crm left in the same response, and Codex (round 2, P1) found any saved run reported ready even when that run had fetch failures; store_status now follows the latest run's failures/tree_complete. Round 6 (2026-10-19, P1): the sql tool's no-such-table and zero-row hints still sent agents to the never-populated resources table; both now name the gz_fleet_* tables, and tools_test.go asserts the corrected hint.

handfixes.summary: --csv, --plain and --quiet output escapes terminal controls (ESC, BEL, C1) in values whatever the writer is (4.35.1's terminalText escapes only on a TTY); tab, CR and LF survive off a TTY for CSV quoting
handfixes.why: Company and endpoint names come from the tenant, and the generated printCSV/printPlain/printQuiet wrote them raw, so a name carrying an OSC 52 or CSI sequence could rewrite the terminal or the clipboard (Codex review 2026-10-19, P1; round 6 P2). scrubCell keeps tab/CR/LF for CSV quoting; quiet output (one value per line) uses cliutil.ScrubTerminal. Same template code in sibling connectors; fleet-wide follow-up.

handfixes.summary: --json, --agent and pretty-JSON output escape UTF-8 C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F) as \u00XX through press 4.35.1's EscapeJSONControls in writeEncodedJSON; the hand-written c1EscapeWriter is retired
handfixes.why: encoding/json escapes C0 controls but writes C1 raw, and xterm/VTE act on UTF-8 C1 (CSI, OSC, ST), so a tenant endpoint name or a quarantined file path in --json, --agent or the default pretty-JSON output could drive the terminal (adversarial review round 7, 2026-10-19, P1). The escape keeps JSON valid and lossless. c1_escape.go is hand-written; root.go wires it in Execute and in the --deliver multiwriter, and helpers.go isTerminal unwraps it so TTY detection is unchanged. Press 4.35.1 escapes C0, DEL, C1, U+2028 and U+2029 inside JSON strings in writeEncodedJSON (every JSON printer), so the stdout/stderr wrapper was dropped at the 4.35.1 reprint; gz_output_escape_test.go pins the behaviour and fails with EscapeJSONControls removed.

handfixes.summary: teach --playbook-file / --playbook-notes-file and teach-playbook --playbook-file / --notes-file are listed in blockedDestinationFlags, so MCP tool schemas omit them and calls naming them are refused; the CLI keeps them
handfixes.why: Over MCP each of these flags reads any file the server account can reach: teach and teach-playbook copy the file into the local learn store, and playbook_list and recall hand it back, in read-only mode too because teach is a local-write tool. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b by driving the real MCP server over stdio with no credentials and a throwaway HOME: tools/call teach_playbook with notes-file pointing at a sentinel file outside HOME recorded it, and playbook_list returned the sentinel text; the other three tool/flag pairs leaked the same way. After the fix tools/list omits all four and each call answers 'unknown MCP parameter' without spawning the CLI. The same probe found 25 of the 30 connectors that ship teach already blocking these flags (by name, by mcp:write-flags or by the usage-text rule); this connector was one of the 5 that did not. Fleet precedent: google-workspace mcp-blocks-local-file-reads. CLI twin checked: teach-playbook --notes-file still reads the file for a local CLI user, which is intended. TestTeachFileFlagsNotSettableOverMCP fails 12 ways on the pre-fix shellout.go and passes after.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (fleet): include the teach family's local-file read flags in the generated blockedDestinationFlags floor.

handfixes.summary: The two derive-lock tests (ContendedAppendIsDerivedBeforeReturn, CaughtUpPassDoesNotWait) wait on what the pass is doing, read from goroutine stacks, instead of fixed 200 ms, 500 ms and 5 s windows; every remaining wait is bounded by the test binary's own deadline
handfixes.why: On windows(fortinet) in CI (2026-10-22, PR #421) the contended test failed with 'contended pass did not finish after the peer released the lock': after release the pass opens a fresh SQLite store and commits, and a slow Windows runner took longer than the fixed 5 s. The 200 ms 'did not return while held' window was also weak: on a slow runner it could elapse before the pass even reached the wait. The contended test now waits until the pass is provably blocked in cliutil.WithFileLock called from DeriveFlagCorrections (it cannot return before release), so it is stronger, not weaker. Proven: a pass that returns early under contention fails it; a caught-up pass that polls or blocks fails the caught-up test; with a simulated 6 s store open after the lock, the old test fails with the CI message and the new one passes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated internal/learn derive_test.go should use this state-based wait in place of the fixed windows.

handfixes.summary: fleet rmm-gap --devices and usage billing --agreements are declared in mcp:write-flags, so the MCP tools omit them and an MCP caller cannot make the server read a file on its host; the CLI keeps both flags
handfixes.why: Both flags name a file the command opens (an RMM device export, an agreements CSV). Mirrored over MCP they let a caller read any file the server account can reach and get its parsed contents back in the result. Found by the msp-skills onboard review after the 2026-10-14 print; carried in the published tree but never recorded in the ledger (found by the 4.35.1 reprint's published-vs-4.33.5-render diff). TestMCPCannotChooseLocalInputFiles fails when either annotation is dropped.

handfixes.summary: go.mod/go.sum carry github.com/inconshreveable/mousetrap, the Windows-only cobra dependency, so GOOS=windows go vet ./... resolves
handfixes.why: The 4.35.1 render's go.sum omits mousetrap (cobra imports it only on Windows), so `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./...` failed with 'missing go.sum entry'. go mod tidy (all platforms) adds it.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal; both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit; every HTTP client (the API client under the GravityZone JSON-RPC envelope, the --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport; every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers; every program file write through the kit (the learn journal through credkit.AppendFile); child processes through credkit.RunCommand and credkit.StartCommand; the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP, and every tool call through credkit.MCPTools. The credential store, config.toml, the legacy config and the Spacefast delivery record are credential sources, written outside the kit by cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile. Every file the wiring holds also has each URL under a base-url or base_url key held through credkit.HoldURL (a profile value under base-url, the base_url the store records), every duplicate key included. A Spacefast page key a publish mints is held the moment its receipt is decoded, and an anonymous page's key-bearing links go only to its record file, whose path is printed instead. Two policy credentials whose JSON name alone is too generic to declare (passwordConfig.value, securityTelemetry.config.key) are held by jsonrpc_transport.go before a result reaches any output. Sites the checker cannot classify on its own are listed with reasons in skills/bitdefender/credkit-sites.json.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own layer. It retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel (replaced by the shared credential kit; the 4.35.1 reprint had already dropped its files, and it is not a `retired` record because check_handfixes.py accepts only registry-backed retirements and fleet_handfixes.json marks that id delegated). Classes closed, each by a test seen failing first on the pre-kit build (internal/credwire/leak_test.go, on the built binaries; BITDEFENDER_LEAK_BIN_DIR runs it against others): credential-bearing read results in CLI stdout and the bitdefender_read MCP result (TestReadResultCredentialFieldsWithheld: license key, push receiver authorization, uninstall password, policy power-user, proxy and password-protection passwords and SIEM key, inventory license key, integration password); the bitdefender_execute confirm preview echoing a password param (TestConfirmPreviewDoesNotEchoCredentialParams); the learn journal recording a held key from argv or BITDEFENDER_LEARN_SESSION (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential); a malformed config.toml's key in either main's startup output, default, --config and BITDEFENDER_CONFIG (TestMalformedConfigCredentialHeldAtStartup); the key sent off the base URL's origin or over plain http, loopback included (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP: --deliver webhook, feedback endpoint, cross-origin redirect, plain-http base URL); a URL saved under base-url in profiles.json (config dir and legacy, duplicate keys and query credentials included) printed by profile show and profile use (TestProfileBaseURLCredentialHeld); the base_url the credential store records printed by the refusal under another --config, in doctor, a command's error and the MCP result (TestStoredBaseURLCredentialHeld); an anonymous Spacefast page's key printed in its private and claim links on publish (TestSpacefastPageKeyNeverPrinted, on the binary, and TestDeliverSpacefastAnonymousKeepsPageKeyOutOfOutput in internal/cli, which also proves the key is held before any output and before a refused receipt returns).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.
